summary: Takeo Hibino was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University (1936–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980).

Takeo Kanaseki was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1949–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1969), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1969–1979).

Takeshi Fujii is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi, later serving as lecturer, professor, and emeritus professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987 to 2021.

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1924–1927). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Sagami Women's University (~1951–1957), and Showa Women's University (~1957–1967), as well as Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University and Nagoya University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1950–1958), and served as president of Chugokugo Gakkai.

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University (~1933–1943), the University of Tokyo (~1947–1966), Seikei University (~1966–1970), and International Christian University (~1970–1976).

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö to serve as Supreme Head of Nyingma (~2012–2015).

Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He held a post at Doho University beginning in 1995 and was affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a research fellowship at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and faculty posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura and others. He held academic posts at Kanazawa University (~1974–1999), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (attested 2004).
Tamara Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023, supervised by Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and conducted postdoctoral work at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung is a historian and Sinologist who earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978), Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994), and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (1994).
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Wang Zhengyi and Renshan Yang (~1896–1898).

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, among others. He taught at Lida Academy and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1970).
Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. She held a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Tandin Dorji is a scholar of history and Tibetology. He has held positions as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College and as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro.
